label: real
what: B1 clock sync: chrony on the Pi against the workstation, and the proof

independent_check.method: ROS header.stamp (written by the Pi) vs receive time (workstation), /scan, 90 s
independent_check.why: the plan's `date +%s.%N over ssh` check has a resolution floor of +/- rtt/2, about +/- 20 ms here, so it cannot see what chrony achieves. A one-way message delay cannot be negative, so the minimum observed stamp->receive bounds the clock offset directly.
independent_check.conclusion: offset(ws - robot) >= -3.0 ms, agreeing with chrony's own -0.5 ms. No scan arrives stamped in the workstation's future, which is the condition that produced the 2026-09-16 message-filter drops.

firewall.finding: ufw is NOT enforcing on either machine
firewall.note: docs said ufw was active on the workstation and the port-123 allow rule was mandatory. The unit is active and enabled; the firewall it manages is off. No rule was needed and none was added.
